title: Weakly Supervised Learning of Nuanced Frames for Analyzing Polarization in News Media
findings: The study found that frames with religious and moral components are a significant part of the political discourse on abortion. For instance, the 'Sanctity of Life' subframe was used substantially more by right-leaning media. The 'Hobby Lobby' subframe, related to religious exemptions for corporations, was also identified as a distinct talking point. The analysis demonstrates that the model can quantify the differential use of these religiously-inflected arguments across the political spectrum, particularly in the context of abortion.

measurement_description: The paper's method measures the usage of nuanced political frames, including those with an explicit religious component, in news media coverage of abortion. Specifically, it identifies and analyzes subframes like 'Hobby Lobby' (corporate religious belief vs. contraceptive mandates) and 'Sanctity of Life' (the holiness of life from a religious and moral perspective).
